We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable disconnections.

The molecule has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl with an NH2 (aniline). Actually structure: .../C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an ortho? Actually it's an aniline (para? not specified). So we have an anilide with free NH2 on phenyl.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also disconnection at amide formation (acid chloride + amine). Also disconnection at the C=C double bond (Heck coupling or Wittig). Simpler: start from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, TsCl) and an aniline derivative (the second phenyl with amide). Actually sulfonamide: we need sulfonyl chloride reacting with an amine (the aniline of the second phenyl). The second phenyl is attached via sulfonyl to the first phenyl? Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) as NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl (para). The sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and also attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc...). So it's a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-aniline (the second phenyl). So we need sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with an aniline (the second phenyl) that already has the side chain (C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So we can first construct the second phenyl with side chain, then sulfonylate with TsCl.

Second phenyl: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . This is a phenyl bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide side chain (cinnamoyl anilide). So we can make that via Heck coupling of 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodo) with acrylamide? Or via condensation (Knoevenagel) of benzaldehyde with malonic acid derivative? Simpler: start from 4-iodophenyl (or 4-bromophenyl) and do Heck with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). But the amide includes an aniline attached to carbonyl; we could form amide later: start from trans-cinnamic acid derivative then convert to amide with aniline.

Alternative: Build side chain via amide formation: start from trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamoyl chloride) reacting with aniline (c3ccccc3N). That gives trans-cinnamoyl anilide (C=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Then attach that to phenyl via Suzuki coupling? Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl via the double bond: the phenyl is attached at the β-carbon of the double bond (the C=C). So the phenyl is the β-aryl of cinnamoyl anilide. That's a trans-β-aryl α,β-unsaturated amide. This can be formed via Heck coupling of an aryl halide (the second phenyl) with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So we need aryl halide (e.g., 4-bromo phenyl) and acrylamide (N-phenylacrylamide). Acrylamide is commercially available (maybe). N-phenylacrylamide (C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1). That's the side chain without the phenyl on the β position. So we can do Heck coupling to attach phenyl.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1: Sulfonamide formation: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) + aryl sulfonamide precursor (the second phenyl with side chain) -> target.

Step 2: Heck coupling: 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodophenyl) (i.e., 4-bromotoluene? Actually the phenyl is unsubstituted (no methyl). So 4-bromobenzene (bromobenzene) as aryl halide + N-phenylacrylamide (acrylamide with phenyl on nitrogen) -> β-aryl α,β-unsaturated amide (the second phenyl with side chain). This yields c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Step 3: Starting materials are commercially available: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, bromobenzene, N-phenylacrylamide. All are cheap.

Check price: TsCl ~ $30 per 100g, bromobenzene ~ $50 per 500ml, N-phenylacrylamide maybe $150. Total far below $9999.

We need to ensure the sulfonamide formation uses the aniline (the second phenyl) which after Heck coupling will have a free NH (the sulfonamide nitrogen). In our target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the second phenyl (the aryl). So the second phenyl must have an NH (aniline) to react with TsCl. After Heck coupling, the second phenyl is still an aniline (has NH2). So we can sulfonylate with TsCl to give sulfonamide linking the two phenyls.

Thus route:

Target (mol) -> Reaction 1 (sulfonylation) using TsCl and intermediate A (aryl amine with side chain). Reaction 2 (Heck) using bromobenzene and N-phenylacrylamide to give intermediate A.

We have only 2 steps (within 3). Provide JSON.

We need template IDs for reactions. We can search for sulfonylation template (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Let's search.
